claims.title: The Federal Charter of the forest cantons
claims.summary: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden sealed a charter of mutual aid against outside lords, refusing foreign judges and pledging to keep the peace; later regarded as the founding act of the Swiss Confederation and its oldest constitutional document.

sources.label: Switzerland: The Swiss Confederation during the Late Middle Ages

claims.title: Battle of Morgarten
claims.summary: Men of Schwyz and Uri ambushed and destroyed a Habsburg army of knights under Duke Leopold I at Morgarten, the first great victory of the Confederation and a celebrated triumph of foot soldiers over mounted nobility.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1315-battle-of-morgarten, claim TL:CHE:event:1315:battle-of-morgarten, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Sempach
claims.summary: The Confederates routed a Habsburg army at Sempach and killed Duke Leopold III of Austria, breaking Habsburg power in the region and confirming the Confederacy as a serious military force.

sources.label: Switzerland: The Swiss Confederation during the Late Middle Ages

claims.title: The Burgundian Wars
claims.summary: Swiss and allied armies defeated Charles the Bold of Burgundy at Grandson and Murten in 1476 and at Nancy in 1477, where Charles fell; victory destroyed Burgundy as a power and made Swiss pikemen the most feared infantry in Europe.

sources.label: Switzerland: The Swiss Confederation during the Late Middle Ages

claims.title: The Confederacy of thirteen cantons
claims.summary: With the accession of Appenzell the league reached its early-modern form of thirteen cantons, a loose alliance of self-governing communities bound by oath rather than ruled by a single sovereign.

sources.label: Switzerland: The Swiss Confederation during the Late Middle Ages

claims.title: Battle of Marignano
claims.summary: A French army under Francis I decisively defeated the Swiss near Milan, the first great Swiss defeat in two hundred years; the Confederates withdrew from Italy, a retreat traditionally seen as the dawn of Swiss neutrality.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1515-battle-of-marignano, claim TL:CHE:event:1515:battle-of-marignano, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zwingli's Reformation in Zürich
claims.summary: Huldrych Zwingli began preaching reform from the Grossmünster in Zürich, launching the Swiss Reformation; the movement won over several cities while the inner cantons remained Catholic, dividing the Confederation by confession.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1519-zwingli-s-reformation-in-zurich, claim TL:CHE:event:1519:zwingli-s-reformation-in-zurich, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Calvin and the Reformation in Geneva
claims.summary: John Calvin began the work that made Geneva the international centre of Reformed Protestantism, deepening the confessional division between the Protestant west and Catholic centre of Switzerland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1536-calvin-and-the-reformation-in-geneva, claim TL:CHE:event:1536:calvin-and-the-reformation-in-geneva, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Peace of Westphalia: independence from the Empire
claims.summary: The settlement ending the Thirty Years' War formally recognised the Swiss Confederation's exemption from the Holy Roman Empire, confirming in law the independence the cantons had long held in fact.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1648-peace-of-westphalia-independence-from-the-empire, claim TL:CHE:event:1648:peace-of-westphalia-independence-from-the-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French invasion and the Helvetic Republic
claims.summary: Revolutionary France conquered Switzerland and replaced the old Confederation with the Helvetic Republic, a centralised unitary state that abolished cantonal sovereignty and the privileges of the patrician towns.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1798-french-invasion-and-the-helvetic-republic, claim TL:CHE:event:1798:french-invasion-and-the-helvetic-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Napoleon's Act of Mediation
claims.summary: After years of factional strife Napoleon imposed the Act of Mediation, restoring a confederal system and creating six new full cantons, including Vaud and Ticino, while keeping Switzerland tied to France.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1803-napoleon-s-act-of-mediation, claim TL:CHE:event:1803:napoleon-s-act-of-mediation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Congress of Vienna recognises permanent neutrality
claims.summary: The European powers declared the perpetual neutrality of Switzerland to be in Europe's interest and guaranteed its territory; confirmed by the Treaty of Paris later that year, this made armed neutrality the foundation of Swiss policy.

sources.label: League of Nations recognizes perpetual Swiss neutrality (Congress of Vienna, 1815)

claims.title: The borders of modern Switzerland fixed
claims.summary: The Vienna settlement restored the cantons and set the Confederation's external borders, which have remained almost unchanged since, leaving curiosities such as the foreign enclaves of Büsingen and Campione d'Italia.

sources.label: The story of Switzerland's federal borders
League of Nations recognizes perpetual Swiss neutrality (Congress of Vienna, 1815)

claims.title: The Sonderbund War
claims.summary: After seven Catholic cantons formed the separatist Sonderbund, the federal army under General Dufour defeated it in under a month with fewer than a hundred deaths, ending Switzerland's last civil war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1847-the-sonderbund-war, claim TL:CHE:event:1847:the-sonderbund-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Federal Constitution
claims.summary: Switzerland adopted a federal constitution that turned the loose confederation into a modern federal state with a Federal Assembly, a collegial executive and a single market, while preserving the cantons; the assembly first met in Bern in November 1848.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1848-the-federal-constitution, claim TL:CHE:event:1848:the-federal-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dunant at the Battle of Solferino
claims.summary: The Geneva businessman Henri Dunant witnessed the carnage of Solferino and organised relief for the wounded, an experience that inspired his 1862 book A Memory of Solferino and his call for protection of war victims.

claims.title: Founding of the Red Cross (ICRC)
claims.summary: A committee of five Genevans took up Dunant's proposals and formed the body that became the International Committee of the Red Cross, adopting the red cross on white — the inverse of the Swiss flag — as the emblem of neutral medical aid.

sources.label: Founding and early years of the ICRC (1863-1914)

claims.title: The first Geneva Convention
claims.summary: A diplomatic conference convened by the Swiss government adopted the first Geneva Convention for the protection of the wounded in war, the foundation of modern international humanitarian law, of which Switzerland remains depositary.

claims.title: Joining the League of Nations
claims.summary: Switzerland joined the new League of Nations, headquartered in Geneva, on terms that its permanent neutrality would be respected, confirming Geneva's role as a centre of international diplomacy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1920-joining-the-league-of-nations, claim TL:CHE:event:1920:joining-the-league-of-nations, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Armed neutrality in the Second World War
claims.summary: Encircled by the Axis, Switzerland mobilised under General Henri Guisan, who rallied the army on the Rütli and adopted the Alpine Réduit defence; the country stayed unoccupied but later faced reckoning over refugees and looted assets.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Switzerland: From a forest-valley oath against the Habsburgs to the armed neutrality at the heart of Europe.", terralore.co/country/CHE/chronicle#ev-1940-armed-neutrality-in-the-second-world-war, claim TL:CHE:event:1940:armed-neutrality-in-the-second-world-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Women win the federal vote
claims.summary: A referendum in 1971 finally granted Swiss women the right to vote and stand in federal elections, one of the last democracies in Europe to do so; the final canton was compelled to follow only in 1990.

sources.label: The long road to women's suffrage in Switzerland

claims.title: Switzerland joins the United Nations
claims.summary: After rejecting membership in 1986, Swiss voters narrowly approved joining the UN in a referendum on 3 March 2002, and Switzerland became the 190th member state that September, while still standing outside the European Union.

sources.label: When Switzerland joined the United Nations

claims.title: A neutral federal republic in the heart of Europe
claims.summary: Switzerland remains a federal republic of twenty-six cantons and four languages, neutral and outside the EU yet enclosing the foreign enclaves of Büsingen and Campione d'Italia, with Geneva a global hub of diplomacy and humanitarian law.

sources.label: The story of Switzerland's federal borders
